transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a harder time thinking through things than I should. It’s probably not a huge thing, but at work I’ll have a test report open, or even just a simple CAD note, and I’ll sit there for like an hour trying to figure out the next sentence or which checkbox to choose. It’s like my brain just stalls out. I don’t know if that makes sense.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your thinking and processing speed?

I think it’s been… about a year or so. It started after I got moved into the prototype-testing role—so, maybe a year and a month ago? I mean, it wasn’t like overnight, but that’s when I first really noticed I was slowing down.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah… I mean, maybe a little. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but things I used to like just feel kind of… effortful now.

Like I have a printer for miniatures, and there’s been this same half-finished figure sitting there for months. I keep thinking I’ll get back to it, but I just don’t. And even yoga, or going for a walk in the woods—things that should help—feel more like tasks I’m supposed to do than things I actually want to do. Does that count?
Would you say you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, more days than not?

I’m not sure I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean… I have off days, definitely, and I probably seem quieter than I used to. But “most of the day, more days than not” sounds like a lot, and I don’t know if I can say that confidently.

Maybe kind of low or flat sometimes? Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed a change in your energy level or felt unusually tired, even when you haven’t been doing much?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’d say unusually tired exactly. I mean, some days I feel kind of worn out, but I usually assume that’s just work or not sleeping perfectly or… normal stuff.

I haven’t really been tracking it, though. Should I be?
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have slowed down, or that you feel restless or agitated without a clear reason?

Maybe a little, yeah. I don’t want to overstate it, but at work I’ve noticed I’m… slower to answer than I used to be.

Like in meetings, people have started finishing my sentences sometimes because I’m taking too long to get the words out or decide what I’m saying. And walking from my desk to the test chamber feels weirdly hard sometimes, like I’m moving through thick syrup. That sounds odd, I know, but… is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that on most days, you feel down or sad for most of the day, even if it’s not severe?

I’m still not totally sure how to answer that correctly. I wouldn’t want to say “most of the day” if that means I’m supposed to be crying or visibly upset or something.

I do feel kind of low sometimes, or muted, but I guess I’ve been thinking of it as stress or just being tired. So… maybe? But I’m not sure I’d confidently say sad most of the day. Does that make sense?
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or felt like you’re not good enough even when others don’t see it that way?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to sound dramatic, because nobody at work is saying this to me, but I’ll make some tiny mistake in the lab and then I keep replaying it over and over.

And it turns into this thing where I’m not just thinking, “I messed that up,” I’m thinking, “I’m bad at this job,” and then… honestly, “I’m just a bad person.” Like whatever consequences happen, I probably deserve them.

I know that may not be a reasonable jump. I’m trying to answer the way you mean, if that counts.
Have you found it harder to make decisions or focus on tasks, even simple ones, more often than not?

Yeah… I think that’s actually a big part of why I came in.

I’m trying not to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s like my brain just… stalls out. I’ll have a test report open, or even something simple like a CAD note, and I’ll sit there for way too long—like an hour sometimes—just trying to decide what the next sentence should be, or which checkbox to mark.

It feels embarrassing because it’s not like the task is complicated. I know what it is, but I can’t seem to move forward with it. Is that the kind of focus/decision thing you mean?
Would you say that most days, you feel a loss of pleasure or interest in things you used to enjoy, even if it's not severe?

Yeah… I think that’s been happening, though I keep telling myself it’s just because I’m busy.

Like, I have this printer I use for miniatures, and it’s had the same half-finished figure sitting there for months. Normally I’d be excited to tweak it or finish it, but I just… don’t. And even things that are supposed to be good for me, like yoga or walking in the woods, kind of feel like another task on a list instead of something I actually want to do.

So I guess yes, most days there’s less interest. I’m not sure if that’s exactly what you mean, but that’s how it feels.
Do you notice that your mood or energy level tends to be worse in the morning and improves as the day goes on?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed a clear pattern like that. Mornings can be hard sometimes, but I don’t know that I reliably feel better later in the day.

It’s more… kind of uneven, I guess. I can try to pay more attention to it if that would be helpful.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently, like eating more or less than usual or gaining or losing weight without trying?

I don’t think so… not in any obvious way.

I mean, I’m probably not eating perfectly, but I haven’t noticed my clothes fitting differently or anything like that. I don’t really weigh myself regularly, so I might be missing something, but nothing has stood out to me as a big change. Is that okay to say if I’m not totally sure?
Have you found yourself feeling like you’re not good enough, or that you’re a bad person, even when others don’t see you that way?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to be dramatic about it, because I know everyone makes mistakes.

But I do get stuck on really small things from the lab. Like if I missed something minor or said the wrong thing, I’ll replay it over and over and it turns into this feeling that I’m not just bad at the job, but… bad as a person. Like I deserve whatever happens because of it.

I know that probably sounds excessive. Other people don’t seem to see it that way, so maybe I’m making too much of it, but that’s where my mind goes.
Would you say that most days, you feel down or sad for the majority of the day, even if it’s not severe?

I don’t know if I’d say the majority of the day most days… that feels a little strong, maybe.

I do feel kind of low a lot, but I’m not always sure whether to call it sad exactly. Sometimes I can still get through what I need to do, so I don’t want to overstate it. But… yeah, there are days where it’s there in the background for a long time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever had a period like this before, where you felt low, slowed down, or lost interest in things for a while, and then it went away?

I’m not sure… I don’t think there’s been a clear period like this before that I can point to and say, yes, that happened and then it lifted.

I’ve had stressful stretches, like anyone, and times where I was tired or not as motivated, but I don’t know if it was the same kind of thing. I don’t want to overstate it if it was just normal stress. Does that answer it okay?
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt down, lost interest in things, or had trouble functioning for at least two weeks in a row, even if it got better later?

I don’t think so… not clearly, anyway.

I’ve had times where I was stressed or kind of run down, but I can’t remember a solid two weeks where I really couldn’t function or completely lost interest and then it passed. Maybe I’m not remembering it perfectly, but nothing obvious comes to mind. Is that okay?
